shows.description: Roy Lichtenstein’s breakthrough Pop work stunned both the art world and the country when it was first shown in the early 1960s. An appropriation artist long before the term was used by art historians, Lichtenstein took his imagery from comic books and newspapers, reconfiguring and refining his compositions before enlarging and transferring them to canvas. shows.title: artport: A History of Internet Art
shows.description: artport: A History of Internet Art marks the twenty-fifth anniversary of artport, the Whitney’s online gallery space for commissions of net art, which launched in 2001. Since its inception, artport has presented a snapshot of the varied practices artists use to engage with an ever-evolving online environment. Taking place online and in the gallery, the exhibition tells a history of the evolution of net art over a quarter century and features more than one hundred works commissioned specifically for artport.

shows.title: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
shows.description: Coumba Samba’s installations draw on forms from the global built environment to expose the social, political, and economic structures they represent. In Stars and Stripes, Samba (b. 2000) uses the geometric shapes and bold colors of modernist abstraction to explore the entanglement of resource extraction with systems of power. Here, sculptures modeled after depleted uranium shells are painted in the colors of the flags of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Namibia, Niger, and the United States. shows.title: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
shows.description: Inspired by vivid dreams and visions, Minnie Evans (1892–1987) made her first drawing in 1935 after the death of her beloved grandmother. During the subsequent decades, the artist created hundreds of radiant pencil and crayon drawings, oil paintings, and collages that combined imagery from her Afro-Caribbean heritage, mythology, religion, popular culture, decorative arts, and the natural environment of her native Wilmington, North Carolina. shows.title: Leo Castañeda: Camoflux Recall Grotto
shows.description: Commissioned for the 2026 edition of the Whitney Biennial, Leo Castañeda’s Camoflux Recall Grotto is a web-based game that prompts players to cultivate a garden in a primordial landscape. Inspired by the Brazilian Amazon forest and South Florida Everglades—as well as works by Colombian artists Maria Thereza Negreiros, Ever Astudillo, and Alfonso Quijano—Camoflux Recall Grotto challenges traditional gameplay. shows.title: Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl
shows.description: The Frick Collection presents an installation of new paintings by the contemporary artist Kent Monkman (b. 1965), whose practice explores historic European art and narratives from an Indigenous perspective. For this project, Monkman takes inspiration from Officer and Laughing Girl (ca. 1657)—one of the Frick’s three paintings by the seventeenth-century Dutch artist Johannes Vermeer—to probe the ways in which it and other artworks of its time represented the effects of global trade and colonization.

shows.title: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450–1500
shows.description: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450–1500 is the first exhibition to focus on Siena as a center of artistic excellence and technical innovation in bronze sculpture during the Italian Renaissance. Bringing together some forty works—many of which have never been exhibited outside of Tuscany—the exhibition invites visitors to appreciate the medium’s beauty and versatility while learning about the complex technical and political challenges that the Sienese bronzeworkers faced.

shows.title: Painting with Fire: Susanne de Court and the Art of Enamel
shows.description: The Frick Collection will present the first exhibition dedicated to the French enameler Susanne de Court. Active around 1600, De Court is an enigmatic figure in the creation of painted enamels. With nearly one hundred surviving works, she is widely believed to have been the only woman to lead a workshop in Limoges, France. This exhibition will bring together around forty-five of De Court’s signed works, inviting visitors to discover her practice and some of the finest examples of her extraordinary output.

shows.title: Vilhelm Hammershøi: Pictures from Home
shows.description: The first major North American exhibition devoted to Vilhelm Hammershøi’s work in more than a decade, this show will focus on the artist’s most celebrated paintings—his series of enigmatic, evocative, and meticulously observed views of the interior of his apartment at Strandgade 30 in Copenhagen. Central themes of the show include the artist’s manipulation of spatial ambiguity; his handling of light, shadow, and temporality; the shifting presence of household objects as they migrated between rooms; and the role of his wife, Ida, as the sole figure featured in several compositions. shows.title: Ruffles & Ribbons: Fashion Plates from the Time of Marie Antoinette
shows.description: Organized in conjunction with Gainsborough: The Fashion of Portraiture, this Cabinet installation presents twenty-four hand-colored engravings that depict French fashion in the late eighteenth century. These plates are selected from Gallerie des modes et costumes français (1778–87), the largest and most influential series of its day. No complete set of Gallerie des modes survives today. Many were discarded when fashions changed, and others could have been destroyed during the French Revolution. shows.title: Gainsborough: The Fashion of Portraiture
shows.description: Gainsborough: The Fashion of Portraiture explores the relationship between works by period-defining English artist Thomas Gainsborough and fashion, a concept and industry that touched nearly every aspect of British society in the eighteenth century.The museum's first special exhibition dedicated to the artist—and the first devoted to Gainsborough's portraiture ever held in New York—this show brings together over two dozen of Gainsborough's most spectacular portraits from across North America and the United Kingdom, representing each stage of his four-decade career.

shows.title: To the Holy Sepulcher: Treasures from the Terra Sancta Museum
shows.description: This groundbreaking exhibition presented more than forty rare objects from the Church of the Holy Sepulcher. These treasures were donated by European Catholic monarchs and Holy Roman Emperors in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries to the church in Jerusalem, the religious center of the Christian faith, and have been safeguarded and used ever since by the Franciscan friars who maintain the site.

shows.title: Mark Bradford: Untitled (A–Z), 2010
shows.description: Mark Bradford’s alphabet builds on an ongoing body of work called “merchant posters,” wherein the artist collects local business advertisements in his South Los Angeles neighborhood. Bradford layers and sands down these once-posted signs—featuring phrases such as “Stop Evictions” and “Affordable Daycare"—abstracting their original messaging so that only fragments remain. The result is twenty-six individual works on paper, each depicting a single letter from the English alphabet.
